QF.id: VII Introduction to Securities Broking Operations_26

question.text: A stock broker can deal with brokers of the same exchange for proprietary trading or client trading only with:

explanation.text: The Logic: A stock broker cannot deal with brokers of the same exchange for proprietary or client trading except with prior permission of the exchange, and after due diligence the exchange allows dealing with only one such broker. The Trap: Dealing with a broker of a different exchange is permitted for proprietary trading after intimation to the parent stock exchange and is again limited to one broker; the same-exchange rule (requiring prior permission) is not satisfied merely by intimation. Note: Same exchange: prior permission of the exchange, limited to one broker. Different exchange: for proprietary trading, intimation to the parent stock exchange, limited to one broker.
